chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Isa from Ibrahim ibn Umar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding His Exalted Saying, 'And whatever you give for interest to increase within the wealth of people will not increase with Allah' (2), he said, 'It is your gift to a man from which you seek a reward greater than it; that is interest which is consumed.'

key_terms.رِبًا: Usury or interest; an increase given in a loan or transaction
key_terms.عِنْدَ اَللّهِ: With Allah (indicating divine accounting or acceptance)
key_terms.لِيَرْبُوَا: To increase or grow (referring to the wealth of the lender)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of riba (interest) in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), riba is interpreted broadly as any excess gift given to secure a greater return, extending beyond fixed interest to include strategic favors. This aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding of 'riba al-jahiliyya' as a mechanism of exploitation, emphasizing that such transactions are spiritually 'consumed' by Allah due to their intent-driven nature rather than just their structural form. The hadith highlights the ethical dimension of commerce, where the purity of intention determines the validity of the exchange.
